title: World Economic Outlook Update, July 2026: Global Economy in Crosscurrents of War and Technology
key_claim: The IMF projects global growth of 3.0 percent in 2026 and 3.4 percent in 2027, broadly unchanged cumulatively from the April 2026 WEO. Growth is uneven, with a war-driven energy shock weighing on energy importers while AI-driven demand lifts economies in the technology value chain. Global disinflation has stalled.
frame_summary: The IMF argues that headline global growth stability conceals a divergence between economies hit by the war and energy shock and those benefiting from the AI upcycle, with stalled disinflation limiting policy room.

title: IMF Data Brief: Currency Composition of Official Foreign Exchange Reserves
key_claim: Total official foreign exchange reserves fell to $13.10 trillion in 2026Q1 from $13.15 trillion in 2025Q4. The US dollar share rose to 57.13 percent from 56.42 percent, with exchange-rate valuation effects accounting for around half of the increase; the euro fell to 20.03 percent and the renminbi edged up to 1.99 percent.
frame_summary: The IMF argues that the dollar's reserve share is broadly stable and that quarter-to-quarter shifts, including the reported gold-versus-Treasuries crossover, are driven mainly by valuation effects rather than active de-dollarisation.

title: 21st package of sanctions: EU hits Russian energy, financial services and crypto hard
key_claim: The Council adopted the 21st package of restrictive measures against Russia on 23 July 2026, imposing asset freezes on 94 banks and major financial institutions, extending the transaction ban to 33 additional Russian credit and financial institutions and 14 crypto-related service platforms, and listing 41 more shadow-fleet vessels. It pauses the automatic oil price cap adjustment until 15 July 2027.

title: Section 122 Global Surcharge Set to Expire July 24 by Operation of Law
key_claim: The 10 percent global import surcharge under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 lapsed automatically at 12:01 a.m. EDT on 24 July 2026, 150 days after taking effect, with no extension legislation pending. Replacement measures were already queued, including a USTR Section 301 forced-labor determination covering 60 trading partners proposing additional duties of 10 to 12.5 percent.
frame_summary: The firm argues that the statutory sunset of Section 122 is a legal formality rather than tariff relief, because uncapped and non-expiring Section 301 and 232 authorities were deliberately sequenced to take over on the same timeline.

title: The dollar is unsinkable for the foreseeable future
key_claim: OMFIF's 2026 Global Public Investor survey found the dollar was the only currency reserve managers as a group planned to reduce exposure to, yet its reserve share has fallen only from around 70 percent to 57 percent over roughly 25 years and reserve managers' average expectation is a 50 percent weight in ten years' time.
frame_summary: OMFIF argues that the dollar's decline in reserve share is real but slow and non-threatening, because incumbency, benchmark captivity and its role as numeraire mean no single currency will replace it.

title: Connector Economies Are Straddling the Global Geopolitical Divide for Potentially Sizeable Gains in Trade

Mexico's inbound FDI reached a record above $41 billion.
